transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (DataHarbor CTO), Leo Carter (ML Eng), Rita Alvarez (Infra)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on benchmark plan and harness integration — discuss customer scripts, load testing approach, streaming vs non-streaming scenarios, success criteria (latency/throughput/cost), and timeline for initial runs. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Success criteria (p95 latency, throughput, SLOs)
- Workload sizing (QPS, avg/burst, seq length)
- Benchmark harness integration (dockerized workloads, wrk/locust, streaming harness)
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs
- Security & data concerns (VPC/KMS/audit logs)
- Timeline and deliverables for POC

Action items (high level):
- Redwood share harness and instructions
- Customer provide representative scripts and data
- Schedule initial benchmark run on Redwood infra

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, alex here, i run the west accounts for redwood inference. priya our SE will walk through the benchmark plan. maya, leo, rita — thanks for making time.
[00:00:27] Maya (DataHarbor): hi, thanks, yea we wanted to lock down how you want us to send our scripts and what success looks like. we're trying to evaluate cost at scale and also keep p95 around 200ms if possible.
[00:00:55] Priya (Redwood SE): cool, thanks. just to confirm, that 200ms target is for streaming or non-streaming? streaming tends to get better perceived latency but the end-to-end numbers depend a lot on token emission and network.
[00:01:20] Leo (DataHarbor): it's for our chat agent flow — so streaming would be ideal, users expect token-by-token. but we'll also measure non-streaming batch generation for comparison.
[00:01:45] Priya: good. so for the POC harness we recommend two tracks: interactive streaming (simulate token streaming) and bulk non-streaming (batch inference). we'll provide a dockerized harness that runs both.
[00:02:12] Rita: quick Q on infra — we are leaning toward private deployment or dedicated? data residency is a big requirement for us.
[00:02:30] Alex: noted — we'll include both hosted and dedicated configs in the plan. for security, we'll send our SOC2 + ISO docs and a short note on VPC/private control plane.
[00:02:58] Maya: perfect, and for benchmarks we want throughput metrics at different sequence lengths: short (16 tokens), medium (64), long (512). cost per 1M tokens is important.
[00:03:25] Priya: that aligns with typical workloads. question on traffic shape — what's your expected qps and burst?
[00:03:40] Leo: baseline qps about 15 req/s for the first phase, with bursts to 120 req/s during peak. average seq len ~40 tokens but p95 spikes up to 300 in some flows.
[00:04:05] Priya: ok that's helpful. for harness we will script a variety of traffic profiles: steady-state qps, short spikes, and a longer ramp test. we use wrk and locust wrappers and a streaming client that opens a SSE/ws and pipes tokens — this will emulate your chat flow.
[00:04:30] Alex: one note — our runtime has prefix/K V cache, batching and quantization profiles; we'll run with your provided scripts both with and without KV cache warm to show delta. sometimes transcripts show K V cash in notes, heh.
[00:04:55] Maya: haha yeah, ok — so can you explain how you compare streaming vs non-streaming in the metrics? we care about perceived latency and also total cost.
[00:05:15] Priya: sure — streaming perceived latency measured as time-to-first-token and p95 of token intervals; non-streaming measured as time-to-last-token. cost measured by tokens + compute time; we'll provide a per-model and per-config cost estimate.
[00:05:45] Leo: will you run models we select or your curated open models?
[00:06:00] Priya: both — we'll run your preferred model variants (you can provide weights or model refs) and we'll run standard open models from our catalog to baseline. if you want private model artifacts, we can host the private deployment or accept a model tarball.
[00:06:30] Rita: security question — KMS integration and audit logs, do you need extra config from our side?
[00:06:50] Alex: we'll share a checklist. for a dedicated or private POC we'll need network peering details and a service account for access; we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. we'll include an onboarding doc.
[00:07:15] Maya: ok good. timeline wise what's realistic?
[00:07:30] Alex: our typical POC for benchmark scoping is 3-4 weeks: week 0 prelim (SOW + access), week 1 harness integration and dry-run, week 2 full benchmark runs, week 3 analysis and follow-ups. with your team's availability we can compress parts.
[00:07:55] Leo: can we get the harness this week?
[00:08:05] Priya: yes — I'll share the harness repo and a dockerfile by end of day tomorrow. it includes examples for wrk/locust and a streaming client implemented in node/python.
[00:08:30] Maya: about the harness — we have complex pre-processing in our pipeline; can we mount our preprocessing containers or do you want us to include preprocessed outputs?
[00:08:50] Priya: best is to provide both: a preprocessed sample dataset plus a wrapper script that runs your preprocessing. our harness can mount customer containers or run an external process; we'll document both.
[00:09:10] Rita: what about load generation — do you want us to generate traffic from our network or have you run it from redwood infra?
[00:09:25] Alex: ideally we run from both sides. Redwood will run a set of runs from our cloud infra to provide a controlled baseline; you should run one of your own runs to validate your network and egress.
[00:09:45] Leo: good. any preferred metrics format?
[00:09:55] Priya: prometheus metrics pushed to a pushgateway is easiest; we also emit CSV/JSON summaries. harness will include a Grafana dashboard template.
[00:10:20] Maya: great. one more thing: regression testing / quality checks — can you tie quality evals to the benchmark? we need to ensure quantization doesn't regress responses.
[00:10:40] Priya: yes we'll run eval prompts/sets you provide and compute a set of quality metrics — e.g., BLEU-ish, accuracy on intent detection, and manual spot checks. we'll flag any quality regression when we test quantized or trimmed models.
[00:11:05] Alex: small aside — sometimes product names get mangled in transcripts, like Redwood Dedicatedy, so i'll attach the glossary to the notes.
[00:11:20] Maya: ok nice. on success criteria, besides the 200ms p95, we want a throughput target of 1000 messages/minute and cost threshold of $X per 1M tokens — we'll put exact number in slack.
[00:11:45] Leo: also operational success: stable throughput with less than 2% error, and autoscaling behavior acceptable during bursts.
[00:12:05] Priya: we'll include error rate and tail-latency checks. for autoscaling we'll run a sustained ramp and observe how the instance pool responds; dedicated configs have different behavior than hosted.
[00:12:30] Rita: can you also show KV cache warmup effects? some of our flows re-use context a lot.
[00:12:45] Priya: yes — harness will run cold-starts and warm-cache runs. we'll capture token latency distributions and cost deltas.
[00:13:05] Alex: ok moving to integration specifics — deliverables we'll send: SOW + pricing, harness repo, security pack, onboarding checklist. customer deliverables: scripts, sample data, model refs, success criteria doc.
[00:13:30] Maya: sounds good. about model refs — we plan to test an open LLaMA variant and a proprietary model; for proprietary we'd prefer a dedicated/private deployment.
[00:13:55] Alex: understood. we'll note that in SOW and include dedicated capacity estimates.
[00:14:15] Leo: any constraints on sample dataset size?
[00:14:25] Priya: for initial runs 5-10k queries is typical; for more robust stats 50k is ideal. streaming tests can use a smaller set repeated to emulate open sessions.
[00:14:50] Maya: ok we'll aim to provide 10k sample queries and a smaller streaming set.
[00:15:05] Priya: on the harness side, you can provide scripts in your preferred language; we include examples in python and js. if you have existing locust scripts, just drop them in and we'll adapt.
[00:15:30] Rita: are there any network prereqs for private deployment?
[00:15:40] Alex: yes, we'll need peering, IP allowlists, and optionally a VPN. full list in onboarding doc.
[00:15:58] Maya: ok. are there any blockers you foresee?
[00:16:08] Priya: only typical ones: delayed script delivery, network peering scheduling, and model artifact access for private models. none are blockers, just dependencies.
[00:16:30] Leo: timeline check — you mentioned initial run 2026-04-09, is that final?
[00:16:40] Alex: tentative, depends on when we get scripts. we should aim to have SOW signed and access granted by 2026-04-02 so we can do harness setup week of 4/5 and first runs 4/9.
[00:16:58] Maya: ok we'll try to meet those dates.
[00:17:10] Priya: i'll also include a short how-to for streaming measurements since they require a slightly different client and metrics.
[00:17:30] Alex: any final questions?
[00:17:35] Maya: one more — will you simulate concurrency inside a session? our chat sessions can have interleaved users.
[00:17:50] Priya: yes we can model session-level concurrency; harness supports session pools that keep kv-cache affinity if desired.
[00:18:10] Leo: excellent.
[00:18:20] Alex: ok recap of next steps: i'll send SOW & pricing, priya sends harness and dockerfile, maya/leo provide scripts and sample data, and we schedule the first benchmark.
[00:18:38] Maya: thanks all.
[00:18:40] (call wraps up; many small clarifications over slack after)

Notes on transcription quality: some minor mis-heard acronyms (SAMEL vs SAML), product names sometimes truncated, filler words present.

Attachments referenced: POC_SOW_template.pdf (link), harness-repo (github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness), security-pack (link to docs), grafana-dashboard-template.json

End of transcript.
